title: BW-PROVIDER-v1 (v1.1)
description: Batch A / A3 — the PROVIDER's own signed descriptor. Until this document, providers were named by URL inside the CUSTOMER's document: `BW-MED.rdp` carries `{discovery, evidence}` and `BW-MED.msp` is a bare URI, both published in the entity's MED and sealed by the entity's key. So a provider serving a thousand entities had its endpoints republished in a thousand documents sealed by a thousand different signers, with nothing stating they described the same provider. A descriptor is the provider speaking for itself, sealed by a key the membership register pins to it (LINT-TRUST-07). BW-MED is NOT changed in Batch A: the endpoints are duplicated for now and the duplication is removed in Batch B, when BW-MED begins referencing participants by identity.

participant_id.description: The participant this descriptor speaks for. The SAME value space the evidence and the membership register use (R7-X1), referenced rather than restated — a descriptor naming a provider in some other notation would be describing somebody the register cannot find.

roles.description: What this provider is admitted AS. `rdp` is the ONE provider role, by decision (SBM-ADR-0015): the Registered Delivery Provider operates the Delivery Service as part of the qualified service it is supervised for. The enumeration was closed to `rdp` in Batch A as a stage, with a second role expected; that second role is withdrawn, and this is no longer a stage. An array rather than a scalar because a participant may hold more than one role should one ever be added.

endpoints.description: The endpoints today scattered across every customer's `BW-MED.rdp`. Same two fields, same meanings; what changes is who says them and who signs.

evidence.description: Evidence-retrieval URI template, `{message_id}` templated as in BW-MED.

expires_at.description: After this instant the descriptor is stale and a verifier MUST NOT rely on it. Compared as an INSTANT (R9-04), never as a string.

kid.description: The key that sealed this descriptor. It MUST be one of the `authorized_seal_keys` the membership register pins to this participant (LINT-TRUST-07) — the LINT-TRUST-05 rule one level up: a seal key authorised for another participant cannot seal this one's descriptor.

ds_receipt_keys.description:
R3-04/R3-T3, moved here by SBM-ADR-0015 (BW-PROVIDER 1.1): the keys that verify this PROVIDER's Delivery-Service delivery receipts. A receipt's `ds_kid` resolves against the issuing RDP's descriptor, pinned by that RDP's membership record — LINT-TRUST-07 already pins the descriptor's seal key, so the receipt key is a published key inside a pinned document and needs no new pin.

It was published on the CUSTOMER's BW-MED, because the Delivery Service was a separate provider and the entity's own signed document was the only place already retained for the evidence period. With one provider role the key is the RDP's own, and a provider's key belongs in the provider's descriptor. The BW-MED path is DELETED, not kept as a fallback: a `kid` present only in a BW-MED does not resolve.

Validity is judged at the receipt's `server_time`, NOT at verification time — that is what keeps an old receipt verifiable after the key that signed it is retired.

kid.description: Unique within this entity's key set; the receipt names it.

alg.description: The COSE algorithm, encoded per the I-D's confirmation-key table (DR-12).

public_key_b64.description: base64, in the one encoding the declared alg defines.

valid_until.description: Exclusive; absent means current. Half-open, as elsewhere.

$comment: SBM-ADR-0015 (BW-PROVIDER 1.1): `ds_receipt_keys` lives here now. Batch A deliberately left it out — "moving the DS receipt anchor off the customer's BW-MED and onto the provider's descriptor is the load-bearing half of Batch B, and doing it here would make an additive batch breaking" — and Batch B was withdrawn with the participant model. The move happens anyway, because it is the RDP's key: what the decision removed was the second provider, not the reason the key belongs to the one that signs with it. This is the breaking half, taken deliberately as a discovery bump.
